skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos through the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.summary: Render Remotion component code into MP4 video output through inference.sh.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Most shell findings are Markdown backticks, tables, or code fences rather than Ruby shell execution. Several examples do instruct users to run belt or npx commands, and the core workflow sends user-provided TSX to inference.sh for remote rendering. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote rendering sends user code and props to inference.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy warning before render examples and tell users not to include secrets, private source, or private media URLs.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends npx commands that install additional skills outside this audit.
remediation.suggestion: Move related skill installs to plain links, or require users to review each external skill before running install commands.

remediation.issue: The required belt CLI and install instructions are external dependencies.
remediation.suggestion: Document the trusted source for belt, authentication requirements, and expected outbound network destinations.

static_findings.snippet: > **Install the belt CLI skill:** `npx skills add belt-sh/cli`

| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |

content.user_title: Render Remotion Videos from React Code
content.value_statement: Programmatic video rendering is hard when animation code must become production MP4 files. This skill sends Remotion TSX to inference.sh and returns rendered video output.
actual_capabilities: Runs the infsh/remotion-render app through the belt CLI.
Accepts Remotion TSX component code with a default export.
Supports width, height, FPS, duration, codec, and props settings.
Uses Remotion APIs such as AbsoluteFill, Sequence, spring, and interpolate.
Provides CLI and Python SDK examples, including streaming progress.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account and the belt CLI.
Sends supplied code and props to a third-party rendering service.
Only documents React, Remotion, and related imports.
Does not provide local rendering or sandbox configuration.

use_cases.title: Automate video generation

prompt_templates.title: Render a data animation

prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python SDK example to render a long Remotion composition and report progress until the final video URL is available.

best_practices: Review TSX before sending it, especially for proprietary code or private media URLs.
Use small test renders before long high-resolution jobs.
Keep render settings explicit: width, height, fps, duration, and codec.
anti_patterns: Sending secrets, private tokens, or unreleased source code inside the component.
Running installation commands for related skills without reviewing their source.
Submitting long renders before validating composition timing with a small sample.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion component code into MP4 video output through inference.sh.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow requires belt login before running render commands.

faq.question: Can I pass custom props?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents a props object that is passed to the exported Remotion component.

faq.question: Which render settings are supported?
faq.answer: The examples show width, height, fps, duration_seconds, composition_id, and codec settings.

faq.question: Does it render locally?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow sends the render job to the infsh/remotion-render app.

faq.question: Should I send private code?
faq.answer: Avoid sending secrets, private tokens, or sensitive unreleased source code to remote render jobs.
